text.p: Following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Government is discussing plans for an administratve reform, cutting costs by 500 million kroons and reducing numbers of MPs from 101 to 71.
- Development Party is facing a split. Arvo Junti resigned on Thursday from the post of chairman to the party board.
- Former Tallinn city councillors have repeatedly violated the law when privatising apartments, auditors said.
- Five participants of the Tartu student demonstration of January 15 were fined some 1000 kroons by the court.
- Scientists have discovered a seven kms wide meteorite crater, the largest in Estonia, in the sea between Osmussaare and Pakri islands.
- Chechenyan community in Estonia recognised Jaanus Raidal's appointment as the representative of Chechnya in Estonia at a meeting.

- Non-citizens who work for police in the Eastern Viru county and who have applied for the Estonian citizenship have been granted another two years to learn Estonian. Only 22 officers would be dismissed, a spokesman said.
- Police prefecture of Harju county is guilty of overspending and signing unlawful property deals, state inspection officials said.
